title: Etli Ekmek
subtitle: Long Konya flatbread with spiced minced lamb
excerpt: Thin yeasted dough rolled into a long oval, topped with minced lamb, tomato, pepper, and onion, then baked until the base is crisp and the edges are golden.
sourceNotes: Konya regional flatbread tradition, central Anatolia. Synthesised from multiple Turkish baking sources.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the baked flatbreads without the topping. Defrost fully and add fresh topping before re-baking at 210C for 10 minutes.
recipe.batchNotes: Make a double batch of dough and topping. Bake in batches on two trays.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The topping can be mixed a few hours ahead and kept covered in the fridge.

content.text: Etli ekmek is a long, thin Turkish flatbread baked with a seasoned lamb topping pressed into the dough. Roll it as thin as you can. A thick base will not crisp properly in the time the topping needs.
Mix the flour, yeast, and salt in a large bowl. Add the water and olive oil. Knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and leave to rise for 1 hour until doubled.

While the dough rises, combine the lamb mince, grated onion, tomato, green pepper, paprika-sweet, paprika-hot, tomato puree, black pepper, and parsley. Mix well with your hands until everything is combined. Set aside.
Heat the oven to 220C. Place a baking tray in the oven to heat up.
Divide the risen dough into 2 equal pieces. Roll each piece on a lightly floured surface into a long oval, roughly 40cm long and as thin as you can manage.
Divide the topping between the two dough ovals. Spread it in a thin, even layer right to the edges. Press it gently into the dough so it stays in place.
Slide the flatbreads onto the hot baking tray. Bake for 18 to 20 minutes until the base is crisp and the topping is cooked through with some browned patches.
Slide onto a board and cut into pieces with a sharp knife. Serve straight away while the base is still crisp.

items.symptom: The base is soggy in the middle.
items.cause: The topping was too wet, or the tray was not preheated.
items.fix: Squeeze excess liquid from the tomato and onion before mixing. Always preheat the baking tray.

items.symptom: The topping is dry and crumbly.
items.cause: The mince was overcooked or the layer was spread too thin.
items.fix: Keep the topping layer at least 5mm thick and remove from the oven as soon as it is just cooked through.

items.cause: It was not kneaded long enough, or it over-proved.
items.fix: Knead for a full 8 minutes until the dough is smooth and elastic. Do not let it rise for more than 90 minutes.
